note: The machine-readable side of the style maps (style-maps.md): the axes a style is described on, the limits review uses for each of its checks with where each comes from, and the map entries a project's `style` may name. An entry's checks override the defaults for the checks on the axes it governs. 'ours' marks a number this project set itself (on its early agent pieces), not a number from a source; per the project's rule a limit is never set on agent pieces again, only from the literature or measured on professional work. A family's or entry's `published_mix` is the published long-term spectrum measurement `analyze` sets the master beside (Pestana et al. 2013's slope over 100 Hz-10 kHz); an entry's replaces its family's, and `borrowed` or `why_none` says why one is lent or absent. An entry's `tempo_bpm` is the tempo range its source gives (its map's tempo cell); `review` asks about a piece whose main tempo lies outside it, a half- or double-time reading counting as inside. A family's `treatments` (0.11) are, by a part's role, the kinds of treatment a published source documents: each with the processing catalog's tools that do it (references/processing-catalog.json), `how` (usual: a corroborated defining convention; often: a source speaks of its frequency; documented: a session or a tutorial), its context, its source (a key of research/effects-0.11's literature notes, cited in the family's map) and `styles` where it holds for some entries only; `none` where the source says the role takes little or none of the kind.

vertical.source: the lengths are ours; the widest distance counted is the minor ninth of the avoid-note rule arrangement.md gives, wider compounds being given apart after Sethares (1993), whose model gives a semitone two octaves wide a quarter of a close one's roughness or less
vertical.what: minor seconds and ninths between a sustained note and another part's note

clash.source: the places are the bar's two strongest metric levels (Longuet-Higgins and Lee 1984); the length and the number asked one by one are ours
clash.what: a counted clash that begins on a downbeat or a half-bar and sounds a beat or more, asked by itself

outside_chord.source: Open Music Theory, Embellishing Tones (the kinds); Longuet-Higgins and Lee 1984 (strong positions); Temperley 2007 (rock melodies leave them unresolved)
outside_chord.what: notes on strong positions outside the written chord, not resolved by step

parallels.source: Open Music Theory, First-Species Counterpoint (the rule, for independent voices); the window and the doubled share are ours
parallels.what: parallel fifths and octaves between lines moving the same way

low_intervals.what: close intervals under their low limit

static_texture.what: every part repeating the same block of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars note for note; with processes_vary, only the runs of the span in which no filter sweep, gain automation or controller curve moves the sound

repetition.what: a part repeating a 1-, 2- or 4-bar cycle unchanged

literal_returns.what: a section repeating an earlier one note for note in every part

arrivals_thinner.what: an arrival section thinner than the one before it in notes per bar, parts or velocity

sections_alike.what: neighbouring sections with the same parts and nearly the same density and dynamics

stiffness.what: chord parts struck and released as one block

unchanging_part.what: a rhythm or harmony part keeping one bar rhythm, and one chord shape where at least half its attacks are chords, over the share of its bars and chords in every section of 4 bars or more in which it attacks in 3 bars of 4, two such sections or more (views.accompaniment); asked where the entry governing the form says its sections differ in texture, or where the plan says a section differs from the one before

pushes.source: Tan, Lustig and Temperley 2019 (rock and pop melodies anticipate strong beats); Witek et al. 2014 (moderate syncopation)
pushes.what: no melody or accompaniment attack anticipating a downbeat or half-bar

restatement.source: Summach 2011 (pop sections state and restate an idea); Caplin 1998 (the sentence); the 8 bars are ours
restatement.what: a section whose melody bars restate no earlier bar's rhythm and shape

melody_durations.what: a melody of few duration values

melody_velocities.what: a melody of nearly flat velocity

transposed_samples.what: notes playing a sample transposed far from its root

highpass.what: a part's high-pass taking from the fundamental of its lowest note

widespread_lowpass.source: Senior 2012 (Sound On Sound, Q&A): widespread low-pass filtering seldom helps a mix and easily dulls it; the 12 kHz (the lower edge of air in the mixing books listed by Moffat, De Man and Reiss 2022), the half and the three parts are ours
widespread_lowpass.what: most parts other than the bass low-passed at or under 12 kHz

tempo_range.source: the tempo ranges the entries' sources give (their maps' tempo cells, `tempo_bpm`); reading half and double time as inside is ours
tempo_range.what: the piece's main tempo outside the range its style entry's source gives

treatment_part.what: a part whose role the map of the style governing the mix documents a kind of treatment for as usual (its `treatments`), while its mix holds no tool of that kind (views.treatment); asked of no family until a rule passes calibration on the 28 projects and paired cases (research/effects-0.11/calibration-treatment.md; Astra's review d011b, point 8): an entry may concern one instrument of the role, as an electric piano's tremolo does
